note: All 365 men's Division I schools inherit the official home-arena source registry. Five researched Arena Files currently include independent, attributed photography and sourced background. Blank fields are not guesses; home arena is not proof of game venue.

84.opened_context: Opened during the 1971–72 season; Branch McCracken Court was dedicated December 18, 1971.
84.history: Opening in 1971, Assembly Hall became the home of three Indiana men's national championship teams. It was renamed and rededicated in 2016 following renovations supported by Cindy Simon Skjodt’s gift.
84.distinctive: Steep seating and a basketball-first atmosphere.

150.opened_context: First opened January 6, 1940, with Duke defeating Princeton 36–27.
150.history: Duke's intimate basketball arena opened in 1940. The packed student section known as the Cameron Crazies is central to its identity, and the arena's classic brick architecture has endured through generations of basketball.
150.distinctive: Close-set stands and one of college basketball's best-known student sections.

photo.title: Interior of Cameron Indoor Stadium, February 2018
photo.author: Nolanwebb
photo.display_note: Taken February 2018. Historic photo, not a live game. Cropped for layout.

153.opened_context: Carolina's first game at the Smith Center was January 18, 1986, against Duke.
153.history: The Dean E. Smith Center opened in 1986 as a new home for Tar Heel basketball. Named to honor coach Dean Smith, the large on-campus building transformed North Carolina's basketball crowd and remains a centerpiece of the program.
153.distinctive: An expansive Tar Heel basketball venue known colloquially as the Dean Dome.

photo.title: Interior of the Dean Smith Center, summer 2006
photo.author: Greenstrat
photo.display_note: Historic summer 2006 interior. Historic photo, not a live game. Cropped for layout.

2305.opened_context: Dedicated March 1, 1955; Kansas beat Kansas State 77–66 in the inaugural game.
2305.history: Named for longtime Jayhawks coach F.C. 'Phog' Allen, the fieldhouse opened in 1955. Modern renovations preserved the building's intimate college-basketball identity while updating fan amenities.
2305.distinctive: The legendary Phog, with a traditional fieldhouse roof and a tightly packed basketball crowd.

photo.title: Allen Fieldhouse during a Kansas–Oklahoma State game in 2006–07
photo.author: Jonnybsay
photo.display_note: Historic 2006–07 interior. Historic photo, not a live game. Cropped for layout.

2509.opened_context: Dedicated December 2, 1967; originally called Purdue Arena and later named for Guy 'Red' Mackey.
2509.history: Mackey Arena opened in 1967 and was renamed in 1972 for Guy 'Red' Mackey. The floor was named Keady Court in 1997, and the arena was rededicated in November 2011 after major improvements.
2509.distinctive: A celebrated Purdue basketball building with Keady Court and an atmospheric enclosed bowl.
